clue.text: Desire clothing but not the ordinary sort

definitions.text: Desire clothing but not the ordinary sort

parts.words: Desire clothing but not the ordinary sort
parts.note: read as a wish for some garment, but the phrase really describes a costume worn for a party, the opposite of everyday wear

explanation.surface: Someone longs for clothes that are a bit out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words read naturally as 'want an outfit'; the answer is literally a verb meaning desire plus a noun meaning clothing, while the whole names a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume worn to a themed party is clothing chosen precisely because it is unlike everyday wear.

clue.text: Hair-raising action by the brave

parts.note: hair-raising normally means terrifying, but here it means literally lifting off hair, the grim trophy-taking once attributed to a warrior, or brave

explanation.surface: A terrifying deed performed by a courageous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective for a bold person; it is the old noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off a defeated enemy's scalp is quite literally an action that raises hair from the head.

clue.text: Sad as the Walrus swallowing first of the oysters

indicators.note: the walrus swallowing something puts that thing inside the walrus word

parts.note: morse is an archaic name for the walrus

indicators.note: first of picks out only the opening letter of the oysters

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of the Walrus from Lewis Carroll's poem gulping down the oysters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Walrus and the oysters come from Carroll's poem 'The Walrus and the Carpenter'; MORSE is an old word for the animal, and O goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes someone sullen and gloomy, a close synonym of sad.

clue.text: Entice one into a club

indicators.note: one going into a club means the letter for one sits inside the club word

parts.note: a bat is a club used to strike a ball
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Lure somebody into joining a club.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait is to tempt or lure, as with food on a hook, which is what entice means.

clue.text: The dogs ran wild, being heedless

indicators.note: running wild suggests disorder, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: The dogs ran off out of control, paying no attention to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the ten letters of THE DOGS and RAN; 'being' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstrong person is wilful and takes no notice of advice, so heedless is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Battle remembered in the long run

definitions.meaning: the Greek victory over the Persians in 490 BC is a battle commemorated ever since
a race of 26 miles 385 yards is the classic long-distance run

explanation.definitionFit: The 26-mile race takes its name from the battle, after the runner who carried news of victory to Athens.

clue.text: Concern for bird

definitions.meaning: in the idiom 'that's not my ...', the word means a person's business or responsibility
a common grey dove of city streets

explanation.definitionFit: Besides naming the familiar dove, the word has an idiomatic sense of someone's affair or responsibility.

clue.text: Lack, on the one hand, all the conclusions

indicators.note: the conclusion of each of the four words is its final letter, and all of them are taken

explanation.surface: Something is missing, on the one hand, when you look at every result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the one hand' sounds like a stock phrase but supplies four words whose last letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a want or absence of something required, the same as a lack.

clue.text: Northern city road

definitions.meaning: the largest city in Alaska, far in the north
roads, or a roadstead, is a sheltered place offshore where ships can lie at anchor

explanation.definitionFit: The Alaskan city's name is also the word for a place where ships moor, which is the nautical meaning of roads.

clue.text: Quick to move, I left in time

indicators.note: I and left being in time means those letters go inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone nimble says they got out with time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: IL (I plus L for left) goes inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and lively, able to move quickly and easily.

clue.text: Appeal — and how the umpire may react?

definitions.meaning: to shout a request or plea
in cricket a fielder appeals and the umpire may respond by declaring the batter dismissed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding side appeals ('Howzat?') and the umpire decides whether the batter is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry for help is a shout to someone, and an umpire who rules a player dismissed is announcing a decision.

clue.text: The cul-de-sac all mortals reach

definitions.meaning: a street closed at one end, with no way through
every living being eventually comes to a final stop when life is over

explanation.definitionFit: A street with no exit is a familiar phrase, and read literally it is the final point every mortal arrives at.

clue.text: Plunge right in, displaying energy

indicators.note: right going in means its letter sits inside the plunge word

parts.note: to dive is to plunge headfirst

explanation.surface: Encouragement to jump straight in and show some vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaying' links the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is the forceful energy and determination to get things done.

clue.text: Yet it's likely to be a slender hope

definitions.text: Yet it's likely to be a slender hope

parts.words: Yet it's likely to be a slender hope
parts.note: the joke is the contradiction between plump and slender: an ironic phrase meaning almost no prospect at all

explanation.surface: A paradox about hopes that are both large and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is used sarcastically to mean the opposite of what it says, which is why it sits against 'slender'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic idiom means very little likelihood, which is exactly what a slender hope is.

clue.text: Hand-to-hand combat?

parts.note: hand-to-hand normally means close fighting with weapons; here it is literally one hand against another, with clenched fists

explanation.definitionFit: Boxing or brawling with bare fists is fighting conducted quite literally with hands against hands.

clue.text: Without hesitation, cutting training

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the cutting word sits outside the hesitation

parts.note: excising means cutting out
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have trained by slicing away without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' wants to mean 'lacking'; here it is the old sense 'outside', so the cutting word wraps round the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising is physical training, working the body to keep it fit.

clue.text: Event in which competitors run until they drop

definitions.text: Event in which competitors run until they drop

parts.words: Event in which competitors run until they drop
parts.note: run until they drop suggests exhaustion, but it is the item balanced on a utensil that drops, ending a school sports day runner's race

explanation.definitionFit: In this children's sports-day race runners balance an egg on a spoon and are out if it falls.

clue.text: An Easter trip to see around Turkey?

indicators.note: a trip as a stumble jumbles these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Suggesting a holiday trip at Easter to see the area around Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like part of the holiday picture but is the anagram signal; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The countries of the eastern Mediterranean region, including Turkey, were traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: No match for a stay-at-home

parts.note: no match suggests being outclassed, but it means a fixture that a homebody would not attend because it is played at the opponents' ground

explanation.definitionFit: A fixture played at the opponents' ground is not a match a home-loving supporter would go to.

clue.text: Running out of clothes

parts.note: suggests having few garments left, but means dashing about naked in public

explanation.definitionFit: The prank of dashing naked across a public place is literally running while out of one's clothes.

clue.text: Payment received by letter

parts.note: suggests money sent through the post, but a letter here is someone who lets property, a landlord collecting money from tenants

explanation.definitionFit: The sum paid for hiring property is what a landlord, one who lets, receives.

clue.text: Numberless Visa bill for a patriarch

indicators.note: the number is the Roman five, and less means it is dropped from the card name

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A credit card statement arrives without a number for an old patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman numeral for five, so 'Numberless' strips the V from the card's name; a bill is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Isaac, son of Abraham, is one of the three patriarchs of Israel.

clue.text: I'm taking a long time making representations

parts.note: ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for spending ages on their portraits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'making' are link words between the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures or likenesses, things that represent something.

clue.text: Poem, an ode concocted in game

indicators.note: the concocted letters are placed inside the game abbreviation

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the usual crossword game

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writing an ode during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges AN ODE, and 'in' puts the result inside rugby union's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a refrain and two rhymes.

clue.text: Stand torture

definitions.meaning: a framework for holding things, such as a plate holder or toast holder
the medieval frame on which victims were stretched

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a holding frame and the instrument of torment, or to inflict great pain.

clue.text: Great moves when used for riot control

indicators.note: the letters of the word move about into a new order

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Approval of a grand manoeuvre deployed to control a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: The irritant spray that makes eyes water is a standard means of dispersing rioters.

clue.text: Job that's OK, oddly

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A piece of work that is acceptable, though a little strangely so.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a job.

clue.text: Stupid fool is after credit

indicators.note: the fool comes after credit, so its letters follow

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ass is a fool

explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly insensitive or dense, a strong word for stupid.

clue.text: She parts company with an angler

indicators.note: she parts the company word, splitting it so it sits within

parts.note: a firm is a business company
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman splits from her partner, who goes fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts company' reads as a breakup, but 'parts' means the woman splits the business word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is someone who fishes with a rod and line, a fisherman.
